installation.note: tar is a built-in command available on all Linux systems by default

overview.summary: tar (tape archive) creates and extracts archive files. Despite its name, it's used for file archiving, not just tape backups. tar can create archives (.tar) and with compression tools (gzip, bzip2, xz) creates compressed archives (.tar.gz, .tar.bz2, .tar.xz). Essential for backups, distribution, and file management.

misconceptions.title: tar compresses files
misconceptions.reality: tar only archives files (bundles them together). Compression is done by gzip (-z), bzip2 (-j), or xz (-J). .tar files are not compressed, .tar.gz files are compressed.
misconceptions.tip: tar = archive (bundle). -z = compress with gzip. tar -czf creates compressed archive.

misconceptions.title: tar requires .tar extension
misconceptions.reality: tar doesn't require specific extensions, but conventions help: .tar (uncompressed), .tar.gz or .tgz (gzip), .tar.bz2 (bzip2), .tar.xz (xz).
misconceptions.tip: Extensions are conventions, not requirements. But use them for clarity: .tar.gz for gzip-compressed archives.

common_pitfalls.solution: Always use -f to specify archive filename. tar -czf (not tar -cz).
Order matters: operation (c/x/t), compression (z/j/J), verbose (v), file (f). Common: tar -czf or tar -xzf.

common_pitfalls.description: Archive extracts to current directory, overwriting files
common_pitfalls.solution: Create directory first: mkdir extract && cd extract && tar -xzf ../archive.tar.gz. Or use -C to specify directory.

related_commands.description: Compress files (tar uses gzip with -z flag)

related_commands.relationship: Archive format; tar for .tar, zip for .zip

best_practices: Use tar -czf to create compressed archives (most common)
Use tar -xzf to extract compressed archives
Use tar -tzf to list archive contents before extracting
Test extraction in temporary directory first
Remember: -f must come last or specify filename immediately after
performance_tips: gzip (-z) is fast compression, good balance
bzip2 (-j) is slower but better compression
xz (-J) is slowest but best compression
Use gzip (-z) for most cases - good balance of speed and compression

additional_notes.common_patterns: Most common: tar -czf (create), tar -xzf (extract), tar -tzf (list). Remember: -f must specify filename.
additional_notes.compression: tar only archives. Use -z (gzip), -j (bzip2), or -J (xz) for compression. .tar = archive only, .tar.gz = archive + gzip.
additional_notes.flag_order: Order: operation (c/x/t), compression (z/j/J), verbose (v), file (f). Common: -czf, -xzf, -tzf
additional_notes.extraction_location: Extracts to current directory. Use -C directory to extract to specific location, or cd to desired directory first
